$comment: CAP: 12 prose entries across expected_shape · read_this_way · suspicious_if ·
blind_spots · decisions · review_notes · expected · known_normal · known_bad ·
do_not_reflag · how_to_investigate · limitations. This file carries 9, and
descriptor.interpretation.entries must equal that number. When a 13th wants in
there are exactly two legal resolutions: PROMOTE it to a check, or DELETE it.
There is no overflow file and no overflow block.
`fences` and `counts` are RECORD blocks, not prose — they are not counted against
the cap. `fences` lives here because the descriptor schema's root is
additionalProperties:false and has no fences category (Spec 120 §14.0).

expected_shape.what: A healthy run of this step SKIPS. The CKAN resource has been frozen upstream since 2022 and every recorded run took the pre-acquisition gate, so the normal audit table is the five `when: "pre"` rows — licence, gate reason, cache validators, dataset age, and the two standing-override rows — with no write counters at all. A full load is the exception, and RAVINE_FORCE_RELOAD is how you ask for one.

measured.query: SELECT count(*), max(started_at), (records_meta->'ravine_load'->>'skipped_reason') FROM pipeline_runs WHERE pipeline = 'sources:load_ravines' GROUP BY 3

read_this_way.what: Every pct row is a RATIO against the PRIOR completed run's feature_count, not against this run's. On a first run — or any run whose prior-run read found no completed row — the prior is null and all four drift ratios are 0 BY DEFINITION, not by measurement. A row of 0 on a first load means 'no baseline to compare against', never 'nothing moved'.

measured.query: SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT source_dataset_version) FROM ravines

suspicious_if.signal: The gate reason reads `no_prior_run` on a database that has run this step before. The prior-run read is scoped to the chain-qualified name `sources:load_ravines` (the #409 correction — the spec froze the wrong string, `source-ravines`, which is never stored), so a rename of the chain or the slug silently detaches the whole baseline and every drift guard degrades to first-run.

measured.query: SELECT DISTINCT pipeline FROM pipeline_runs WHERE pipeline ILIKE '%ravine%'

suspicious_if.signal: A full load reports inserted + updated = 0 while polygons_deleted is also 0 and the content hash CHANGED. Under a role that does not bypass RLS the upsert and the delete both affect zero rows with no error, which is byte-identical to an unchanged source; the privilege row is what tells the two apart.

measured.query: SELECT c.relrowsecurity, (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_policy p WHERE p.polrelid = c.oid), (SELECT rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user) FROM pg_class c WHERE c.oid = 'ravines'::regclass

blind_spots.what: Geometry is validated for TYPE and validity, never for PLACE. A publisher that shipped the same 854 well-formed polygons translated by a kilometre would pass every check here: the count is unchanged, nothing needs repair, nothing departs. Only the downstream in-ravine rates would move, and nothing in this step reads them.

measured.query: SELECT round(100.0*count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_in_ravine_protection_area)/count(*), 2) FROM parcels

blind_spots.what: The pre-acquisition gate compares HTTP cache validators only, so a publisher that re-stamps last-modified without changing a byte still costs the whole download. The content-hash gate eats the parse and the write but not the transfer — it cannot, because it needs the bytes to hash them.

Nothing here observes a process kill. The ledger strand window closes THROWN errors only; a SIGKILL or an OOM inside the download window leaves the pipeline_runs row `running` and no check can see it — and a stranded `running` row is exactly what a downstream `status = 'completed'` gate reads as absent.

measured.value: 0 checks cover process death; the window is a `finally`

decisions.what: Geometry validation uses this step's own batched VALUES+UNNEST SQL (now scripts/lib/step/write.js GEOMETRY_VALIDATION_SQL), NOT the shared scripts/lib/geometry-validator.js.
decisions.why: DEC-B. The shared helper cannot emit the geometry_collection_extracted counter, and Spec 59 §9 froze that counter into the producer contract — so adopting the helper would silently drop a field a consumer is entitled to read. The divergence is deliberate and has to stay visible, because 'why isn't this using the shared validator' is the first question every reviewer asks.

decisions.what: SPEC_VERSION stays '1.2' even though the Spec 59 header reads v1.3.
decisions.why: enrich-ravines.js:42 pins the value EXACTLY and HALTs the sources chain on anything else. The pin is the contract; the document's version number is documentation. Bumping it to match the header would look like tidying and would stop the chain.

fences.const: the L7c mass-delete terminal — `deleted / prior_feature_count` over the declared bound is a FAIL row AND the run ends `failed`, unless RAVINE_ACCEPT_MASS_DELETE is standing
fences.value: check ravine_mass_delete_pct (limit_from_config load_ravines_mass_delete_fail_pct, default 0.5) + override.accept_anomaly[RAVINE_ACCEPT_MASS_DELETE]; the override moves the STATUS, never the row
fences.incident: Severity HIGH, recorded in the commit's own footer: the mass-delete abort was NON-FUNCTIONAL before review — the row was pushed but nothing gated the outcome on it, so a run that retracted most of the ravine layer completed green and enrich_ravines was protected only by its own read of mass_delete_check_passed.

fences.const: the tier-2 content-hash gate over a STREAMED md5 hash-through-to-disk — contentHashDecision + tier2 + buildSkipReEmitMeta, and never a whole-buffer download or a whole-file read
fences.value: staleness.trigger[content_hash @ post_acquisition], md5 pinned; the tier-2 skip re-emits the prior block so the run still lands a `completed` row (DS4)
fences.incident: Severity HIGH. Two failures in one commit: the archive was buffered entirely into memory before hashing (Spec 43 §9.5 bans it — the same pattern on the 327 MB parcels CSV is an OOM), and every metadata re-stamp by CKAN forced a full re-parse and 854 no-op upserts because nothing compared the bytes. Reverting either is invisible in the outputs, which is why the lock reads the code.
